gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices for ChatGPT's two budget picks: the GardePro A3S is $71.99 at gardepro.com, below the $95 TechGearLab listed, and the Spypoint FLEX-M2 is $79.99 at spypoint.com with a free plan of 100 photos per month. That makes both about half the price of the $149.95 Bushnell Core S-4K that ChatGPT picked first.
standout_why: Pages compared: Outdoor Life best trail cameras (2026-10-19) and TechGearLab best trail camera (2026-08-18). TechGearLab lists the A3S at '$95 (on sale)' and covers the older Spypoint Flex-M at $130, not the FLEX-M2. Outdoor Life does not cover the A3S or the FLEX-M2 and only links to 'SpyPoint Flex'. ChatGPT's own answer shows no price for either budget card. No cited page has the FLEX-M2 at $79.99 or the A3S at $71.99. Popular Mechanics and Wirecutter could not be opened (fetch blocked or not tried within budget), so they were not checked.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's choices but adds the missing numbers. Without a subscription, the A3S at $71.99 costs $77.96 less than the Core S-4K at $149.95. The catch is that TechGearLab rated the A3S trigger 'below average', against the Bushnell's 0.2 s spec. For phone delivery, the FLEX-M2 at $79.99 with a free 100-photo/month plan undercuts the Tactacam REVEAL Pro 4.0 Solar (about $200 per Outdoor Life, plans from $5/month) for a buyer who doesn't need solar. Our own GardePro E8 3.0 Pro and E9 3.0 Pro, both $119.99, sit between these two tiers as Wi-Fi models with no data plan.
